blocks.text: We have learned that when microbes attack body, macrophages provide the immediate response by engulfing them. This response cannot eliminate many microbes, but it gives time for the immune system (third line of defence) to respond.

When a macrophage engulfs a microbe, it also produces special proteins for the helper T cells. When the helper T cells recognize these proteins through their receptors, they are activated. The activated helper T cells initiate two parallel immune responses i.e., cell-mediated immunity, and antibody-mediated immunity.
